tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$env:DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

7: 1. Executive Summary & PM Overview
8: As Project Manager of group CTRL+STAY, I have prepared this formal technical report detailing the system architecture, hardware topology, software stack selection, and offline communication protocols for VenueVue. VenueVue is an offline-first Point-of-Sale (POS) and recipe-based inventory management system custom-engineered for TravelBean MNL—a mobile pop-up coffee venture operating out of Tondo, Manila.
9: Mobile pop-up coffee setups face acute technical constraints: event venues (such as outdoor fairs, school grounds, and weddings) frequently operate in cellular dead zones or congested wireless environments where online, cloud-dependent POS systems fail completely. VenueVue directly resolves this bottleneck by implementing a self-contained local client-server network that operates with 100% functional reliability in off-grid environments without internet connectivity.

As of September 22, 2026, group CTRL+STAY has successfully achieved the 20% Phase 1 Milestone. The local development host environment is fully configured on XAMPP (PHP 8.x and MySQL 8.x), the 6-table relational database schema is established with strict foreign keys, role-based access control (RBAC) security frameworks are active, and client-side UI design tokens are established. Prepared by: Zapico, Zaki (Project Manager & Lead Developer, Group CTRL+STAY)

As Project Manager of group CTRL+STAY, I have prepared this formal technical report detailing the system architecture, hardware topology, software stack selection, and offline communication protocols for VenueVue. VenueVue is an offline-first Point-of-Sale (POS) and recipe-based inventory management system custom-engineered for TravelBean MNL—a mobile pop-up coffee venture operating out of Tondo, Manila.

Mobile pop-up coffee setups face acute technical constraints: event venues (such as outdoor fairs, school grounds, and weddings) frequently operate in cellular dead zones or congested wireless environments where online, cloud-dependent POS systems fail completely. VenueVue directly resolves this bottleneck by implementing a self-contained local client-server network that operates with 100% functional reliability in off-grid environments without internet connectivity.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+| PROJECT PROGRESS SNAPSHOT: PHASE 1 MILESTONE (20% COMPLETED)                      ||                                                                                   ||  [X] Local XAMPP Server Environment (Apache, PHP 8.x, MySQL 8.x)                  ||  [X] Relational Database Schema (6 Core Entities with Foreign Key Constraints)    ||  [X] Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) Security Setup (password_hash)              ||  [X] UI Design Tokens & Foundations (Tailwind CSS 4)                              ||  [> ] Active Task: Authentication Routing & Navigation Flows (React 19 SPA)       |+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Our team remains strictly aligned with the CEIT academic calendar, running from August 3, 2026, to December 18, 2026. As of September 22, 2026, group CTRL+STAY has successfully achieved the 20% Phase 1 Milestone. The local development host environment is fully configured on XAMPP (PHP 8.x and MySQL 8.x), the 6-table relational database schema is established with strict foreign keys, role-based access control (RBAC) security frameworks are active, and client-side UI design tokens are established. Our active development focus centers on finalizing client authentication routing and dashboard navigation flows.
VenueVue utilizes a modified Three-Tier Client-Server Architecture deployed strictly within a local, offline star topology.

(192.168.137.1) -- Sits safely under counter              ||   * Windows Mobile Hotspot Broadcaster                                            ||   * Local XAMPP Web Server (Apache HTTP Engine) (line truncated to 2000 chars)

Executing directly within the browser (or installed as a full-screen Progressive Web App / Kiosk WebView) on mobile tablets, the front-end is engineered as a Single Page Application (SPA) using React 19, TanStack Router, Vite 8, and Tailwind CSS 4. It handles touch-optimized UI rendering, real-time cart calculations, category tab filtering, client-side input validation, and temporary browser session storage without triggering full page reloads.

Hosted locally on the laptop workstation via an offline XAMPP Apache web server, this tier executes back-end logic written in PHP 8.x. It serves the compiled static React SPA assets to connected client tablets, validates API authentication requests, enforces role-based security, executes the recipe deduction algorithms upon transaction completion, manages offline data sync ingestion, and powers the automated spreadsheet export engine.

Consisting of a local MySQL 8.x relational database, this tier guarantees transactional data integrity across 6 core relational tables: USERS, PRODUCTS, INGREDIENTS, RECIPE_ITEMS, ORDERS, and ORDER_ITEMS. All database interactions utilize PHP Data Objects (PDO) with Prepared Statements to eliminate SQL injection vulnerabilities.

To eliminate 2 to 3 hours of late-night manual calculator sales tallying and post-event administrative burnout, VenueVue integrates the open-source PhpSpreadsheet library (v1.28+) directly into its PHP back-end.

When the owner triggers the export function on either the host laptop or the Mobile Admin Tablet, the system queries the local MySQL database, aggregates transaction records, and compiles a pre-formatted, publication-ready multi-tab Excel workbook (.xlsx) in under 10 seconds.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+|                     AUTOMATED 4-TAB EXCEL WORKBOOK (.XLSX)                        |+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+|  [TAB 1: SUMMARY]                                                                 ||   * Event Name, Date, Duration, Total Gross Revenue, Net Profit Estimates         ||   * Total Order Count, Average Order Value (AOV), Primary Payment Distribution    |+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+|  [TAB 2: SALES BY PRODUCT]                                                        ||   * Itemized breakdown of drinks and pastries sold                                ||   * Product Category, Volume Sold, Unit Retail Price, Total Revenue per Item      |+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+|  [TAB 3: INGREDIENT USAGE]                                                        ||   * Raw Material Depletion Metrics (e.g., Coffee Beans in g, Milk in mL)          ||   * Initial Stock vs. Depleted Quantity vs. Remaining Ending Inventory Balance     |+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+|  [TAB 4: RESTOCK LIST]                                                            ||   * Automated procurement recommendations                                         ||   * Filters items that breached configured minimum stock thresholds                |+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
Commercial POS options were evaluated during our initial research phase. The table below summarizes the technical rationale for building VenueVue over adopting commercial cloud or retail solutions:

While Lavu POS offers ingredient tracking, its reliance on internet connectivity and monthly subscription costs make it unsuitable for micro pop-up coffee vendors. Local mobile apps like Peddlr POS track inventory only as discrete units (e.g., selling 1 canned beverage deducts 1 unit), making them incapable of tracking assembled coffee recipes. VenueVue bridges this gap specifically for the pop-up coffee market.
3.2 Justification for Local Wi-Fi Hotspot Topology (192.168.137.x)
To achieve complete offline independence, the host laptop activates Windows Mobile Hotspot to broadcast a local wireless star topology.
Zero External Router Dependencies: The host laptop acts as the wireless access point and DHCP server, eliminating the need to transport, power, and configure external routers at pop-up venues.

Deterministic Subnet Addressing: The host laptop takes static IP 192.168.137.1, while client tablets receive leases within the 192.168.137.100+ range. Client API endpoints explicitly target 192.168.137.1, guaranteeing instant HTTP routing across devices without internet access.
3.3 Recipe-Based Inventory Deduction Logic vs. Basic Item-Level Tracking

Standard retail POS software deducts inventory on a 1-to-1 product basis. In a specialty coffee pop-up, preparing a single 16oz Iced Salted Caramel Latte simultaneously consumes multiple raw materials:

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+| RECIPE DEDUCTION ALGORITHM EXECUTION                                              |+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+|  1. Barista submits order for 1x [16oz Iced Salted Caramel Latte]                 ||  2. System queries [RECIPE_ITEMS] junction table for Product_ID                   ||  3. System identifies required raw ingredients & quantities:                       ||     - Ingredient #101 (Espresso Beans) -> Deduct 18.00 g                          ||     - Ingredient #102 (Full-Cream Milk) -> Deduct 200.00 mL                        ||     - Ingredient #103 (Caramel Syrup)  -> Deduct 30.00 mL                         ||     - Ingredient #201 (16oz Cup)       -> Deduct 1.00 unit                        ||  4. SQL UPDATE query executes against [INGREDIENTS] table in single transaction     ||  5. Remaining stock evaluated against Min_Stock_Threshold                         ||  6. If Current_Stock <= Threshold, trigger visual low-stock alert flag            |+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
3.4 Front-End Stack Selection Rationale (React 19 SPA vs. Flutter APK)

During early planning, native cross-platform mobile frameworks (e.g., Flutter builds) were considered. However, deploying compiled APK files across multiple tablets during fast-paced event setups creates operational friction: native APKs require manual side-loading, introduce OS version mismatches between Android tablets and iPads, and require physical USB access to roll out code updates.
Transitioning to a client-rendered Single Page Application (React 19, TanStack Router, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS 4) served locally via XAMPP provides distinct operational advantages:

Single-Source Updating: Pushing a new production build (dist folder) onto the host laptop updates the entire application across all barista and admin tablets simultaneously upon browser refresh—eliminating individual tablet USB updates.
Universal Compatibility: Tablets connect instantly via Chrome or Safari regardless of operating system.

Native APK Look and Feel: By adding the application to the tablet home screen via Progressive Web App (PWA) manifest or launching it within an Android Kiosk WebView container, the app runs in full-screen standalone mode without browser address bars—delivering the performance and feel of a native APK.

Client tablets communicate with the XAMPP back-end via standard HTTP REST request/response cycles over the local wireless hotspot (192.168.137.x). When a barista completes a transaction, the tablet constructs a lightweight JSON payload containing order metadata, line items, cash tendered, and timestamps, sending it via HTTP POST to the laptop's PHP API endpoint.
To accommodate varying venue conditions and emergency failure recovery, VenueVue implements three distinct post-event data synchronization protocols:

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+| MULTI-PROTOCOL DATA SYNCHRONIZATION ARCHITECTURE                                  |+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+|                                                                                   ||  [METHOD 1: LOCAL WI-FI PUSH] (Primary Real-Time Protocol)                        ||   Tablets push JSON order payloads over HTTP to 192.168.137.1 during active sales. ||                                                                                   ||  [METHOD 2: DIRECT USB CABLE / DRIVE TRANSFER] (Secondary Fail-Safe)              ||   If Wi-Fi fails, transaction logs cached on tablets are exported as .sql/.json   ||   files and transferred to the host laptop via USB drive.                         ||                                                                                   ||  [METHOD 3: STRUCTURED EXCEL / CSV IMPORT] (Manual Fallback Ingestion)            ||   Sales spreadsheets exported from tablets are uploaded into the laptop's         ||   administrative import module, which parses records using PhpSpreadsheet.        ||                                                                                   |+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
To prevent data loss or database corruption during high-volume event rushes, VenueVue enforces strict fail-safe mechanisms:

Session Auto-Caching: The client-side React 19 app automatically caches active cart states and uncommitted transactions in the tablet's browser local storage every 5 transactions. If a tablet battery dies or the browser closes accidentally, the barista reopens the app to restore the pending order state.

Network Disconnection & Retry Logic: If the Wi-Fi connection drops, the client app pauses background syncing and retains transactions locally. It executes an exponential backoff retry loop (up to 3 attempts). If connectivity remains unestablished, the owner seamlessly switches data ingestion to USB Transfer (Method 2) or Excel Import (Method 3).

Primary Key Collision Prevention: Every transaction is assigned a globally unique identifier combining the Tablet ID and a sequential integer (e.g., T1-0104). If a duplicate key is detected during file imports, the ingestion script automatically pauses, flags the duplicate record, and prompts administrative review before merging.

Atomic File Parsing: All batch file imports execute within atomic MySQL transactions (START TRANSACTION ... COMMIT). If a parsing error occurs mid-file, the system issues an immediate ROLLBACK, leaving the database in its prior state.
Automated Database Backups: The system generates daily .sql database dumps stored on the host laptop's internal drive and automatically mirrored to an external 64GB USB flash drive.

This technical specifications overview provides the structural foundation for the VenueVue implementation plan. It maintains full alignment with our 20% milestone progress while establishing clear protocols for upcoming development phases.

Mobile pop-up coffee ventures operating in temporary physical venues—such as outdoor fairs, private weddings, school grounds, and corporate pop-ups—face severe operational friction due to complete reliance on manual paper sales tracking, post-event calculator sales tallying, and unmonitored raw material consumption. Because event venues frequently operate in cellular dead zones or congested wireless environments, cloud-dependent Point-of-Sale (POS) systems become completely unusable. Furthermore, standard retail POS software tracks finished goods as discrete units rather than raw materials, leaving operators unable to monitor recipe depletion (e.g., deducting espresso beans in grams, full-cream milk in milliliters, and paper cups in units per beverage sold).
A quantitative SWOT and problem-prioritization analysis conducted by group CTRL+STAY with TravelBean MNL identified seven core operational problems:
| Total absence of an offline POS system
| Forces paper-based order entry; leads to miscalculated totals and lost order slips.
| Requires 2 to 3 hours of manual calculation per event; causes operator burnout.
| Tallying paper receipts using handheld calculators.
| Frequent mid-event stockouts of essential items (espresso beans, full-cream milk, cups).

| Staff remain unaware when raw materials reach critical thresholds, causing rejected orders.

VenueVue is an Internet-independent, locally networked, offline-first Point-of-Sale (POS) and recipe-driven inventory management system custom-engineered for mobile pop-up coffee shop operations. The system utilizes an edge host server consisting of Apache, PHP 8.x, and MySQL 8.x on a central host laptop, communicating with client tablets through a local Wi-Fi LAN using the 192.168.137.x subnet range.

Operational Availability Definition: VenueVue provides operational availability independent of WAN/Internet access, provided that the local host server and local wireless network remain active. "Offline" in this study refers specifically to the absence of WAN/Internet connectivity, not complete autonomous operation of every individual tablet. The system relies on the local host server for authoritative transaction processing, recipe inventory computation, RBAC session validation, and database persistence.
Single Operational Dependency & Failure State Handling
While VenueVue operates without WAN/Internet access, it relies on the local edge host laptop. The system behavior under distinct network failure conditions is explicitly defined:

SYSTEM FAILURE STATE DIAGRAM                       [ WAN / Internet Loss ]                [ Edge Host Server Failure ]               │                                         │               ▼                                         ▼   Wi-Fi LAN & Host Server Active            Local API Processing Halted               │                                         │               ▼                                         ▼   100% Full POS Operations Active           Tablets Shift to Local Queue   (Direct Wi-Fi Ingestion)                  (IndexedDB / USB Export Package)
WAN / Internet Failure: System remains 100% operational. Tablets submit transactions directly to the local server via Wi-Fi.

Local Host Server Failure: Server-side transaction processing becomes unavailable. Client tablets transition to queueing transactions locally in IndexedDB as PENDING_LOCAL until server recovery or USB physical package export.

| Digitally capture customer transactions at POS.

| $A_{deduction} = 100.00\%$ precision between theoretical BOM depletion and database updates.

| Guarantee Internet-independent system availability during mobile events.
| 100% operational availability independent of WAN/Internet connectivity.
| Automate post-event sales and operational report generation.
| Multi-tab Excel workbook (.xlsx) generated in $T_{export} \le 10 \text{ seconds}$ post-event.
| Enable flexible multi-device data ingestion post-event.
| Enforce API-level Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) across devices.
| Strict backend HTTP 401/403 rejection on unauthorized API calls.

VenueVue utilizes a modified Three-Tier Client-Server Architecture deployed within a local wireless star topology broadcast by the host laptop (192.168.137.1).

VENUEVUE              INTERNET-INDEPENDENT EDGE POS                         │          ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐          │                             │     CLIENT TIER                   EDGE HOST (React 19 SPA/PWA)              (Apache / PHP 8.x)          │                             │  IndexedDB Queue                Authentication  Touch POS Interface            RBAC Authorization  Local State Machine            Idempotency Layer          │                      Recipe Engine          │                      Inventory Engine          │                      Export Engine          │                             │          └───────── Local Wi-Fi ───────┘                        │                     MySQL 8.x                  (InnoDB Engine)                        │        ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐        │               │               │     ORDERS        INVENTORY_        AUDIT_LOGS    / ITEMS       TRANSACTIONS        │   RECIPE_ITEMS        │   INGREDIENTS
Presentation Tier (Client): Executes in tablet browsers or PWA Kiosk mode. Manages touch UI, cart state, client validation, and local IndexedDB transaction queueing during network partitions.

Application Tier (Business Logic): Hosted on Apache/PHP 8.x via XAMPP. Serves static React assets, validates session tokens, enforces RBAC permissions, executes atomic recipe deductions, handles idempotency, and compiles Excel exports.
Data Persistence Tier (Database): MySQL 8.x running on the InnoDB engine. Maintains ACID-compliant relational storage across 8 core tables using prepared statements.
VenueVue replaces "synchronization protocols" with three defined data-ingestion mechanisms pointing to the authoritative database:
Mechanism 1 — Real-Time Wi-Fi HTTP POST (Primary): Client tablets submit completed order payloads over the local hotspot network (192.168.137.x) to the PHP API.

Mechanism 2 — Local IndexedDB / USB Recovery Import (Fail-Safe): When Wi-Fi drops, transactions queue locally in IndexedDB under a PENDING_LOCAL state. Queued records can be exported as structured JSON recovery packages and transferred via USB drive to the host laptop.

Mechanism 3 — Manual Excel/CSV Batch Ingestion (Administrative Fallback): Sales spreadsheets uploaded via the Mobile Admin Console are parsed using PhpSpreadsheet, verified against idempotency keys, and committed atomically.
Every tablet-generated order receives a client-generated UUIDv4 client_transaction_id before transmission.
The database enforces a UNIQUE index constraint on ORDERS.client_transaction_id. Upon receiving a request:
The PHP API checks if client_transaction_id already exists in ORDERS.
If it exists, the server returns the existing transaction result without re-executing inventory deductions.
If new, the server executes the atomic transaction and returns 201 Created.
The client updates the local status to COMMITTED only after receiving the server's HTTP confirmation.

When multiple barista tablets submit orders simultaneously, inventory deduction is protected against race conditions using InnoDB row-level locking (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) inside a single database transaction:

The database schema is expanded to 8 core tables to guarantee inventory movement traceability and security auditability:
USERS: user_id (PK), username (UNIQUE), password_hash, role (ENUM: BARISTA, OWNER), is_active, created_at.
PRODUCTS: product_id (PK), product_name, category, unit_price, is_active.
INGREDIENTS: ingredient_id (PK), ingredient_name, unit (g, mL, units), current_stock, minimum_stock, updated_at.
RECIPE_ITEMS: recipe_item_id (PK), product_id (FK), ingredient_id (FK), quantity_required. Constraint: UNIQUE(product_id, ingredient_id).
ORDERS: order_id (PK, BIGINT), client_transaction_id (CHAR(36), UNIQUE, NOT NULL), user_id (FK), tablet_id, total_amount, cash_tendered, created_at, committed_at.
ORDER_ITEMS: order_item_id (PK, BIGINT), order_id (FK), product_id (FK), quantity, unit_price.

INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS: inventory_transaction_id (PK, BIGINT), ingredient_id (FK), user_id (FK), order_id (Nullable FK), transaction_type (ENUM: SALE, RESTOCK, ADJUSTMENT), quantity_delta, reason, created_at.
AUDIT_LOGS: audit_log_id (PK, BIGINT), user_id (Nullable FK), action, entity_type, entity_id, details (JSON/TEXT), ip_address, created_at.

Security is enforced strictly at the PHP API level. Hiding UI buttons in React is treated as a UX feature, not authorization. Every API request must validate the user's session token and role permissions, returning HTTP 401 Unauthorized or HTTP 403 Forbidden if unauthorized. All administrative overrides, restocks, and security rejections are logged in AUDIT_LOGS.
The evaluation of VenueVue is governed by explicit mathematical formulas:
Measures absolute precision between calculated mathematical stock depletion ($Q_{BOM}$) and physical database updates ($Q_{DB}$) across $n$ evaluation observations:
Measures turnaround time between client transmission ($t_{submit}$) and server database confirmation ($t_{commit}$):
(Target: Mean $L_{trans} \le 250 \text{ ms}$, 95th Percentile $p95 \le 500 \text{ ms}$ on local LAN).
Evaluates data restoration completeness following a network partition ($N_{queued}$ transactions queued locally):
| Successful commit; $L_{trans} \le 250 \text{ ms}$ on local Wi-Fi.
| Zero lost updates; sequential atomic transaction commits.
| Multiple tablets selling items sharing ingredients
| Transaction retained safely in tablet IndexedDB as PENDING_LOCAL.
| $R_{sync} = 100\%$; queued transactions automatically reconcile to host.
| Network timeout followed by client retry
| $R_{duplicate} = 0\%$; UUID constraint prevents duplicate order creation.
| Import module flags existing UUIDs and skips re-deduction.
| Valid records committed atomically; malformed rows trigger rollback.
| PHP API returns HTTP 409 Conflict; inventory remains untouched.
| Barista account calling stock edit API endpoint
| Backend returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; logged in AUDIT_LOGS.
| Transmitting API payload with expired session
| Backend returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized; operation blocked.
| Recipe BOM verification across menu items
| Calculated recipe quantities exactly match INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS.
| Interface renders low-stock badge; item listed in Restock List.
Academic Schedule: August 3, 2026 – December 18, 2026 (20 Weeks / 5 Months)
Status Snapshot: Phase 1 Milestone (20% Completed) as of September 22, 2026.
Implementation follows a strict dependency path. No higher-tier feature is built before its underlying persistence and security foundations are frozen:
| Product, Ingredient, and Recipe CRUD Modules
| IndexedDB Local Queue & UUID Idempotency Engine
| USB Recovery Package & CSV Ingestion Engine
7.1 Direct Outlays vs. Imputed Software Valuation
Software Licensing: ₱0.00 (All software layers—React 19, TanStack Router, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS 4, PHP 8.x, MySQL 8.x, XAMPP, PhpSpreadsheet—operate under open-source licenses).
Hardware Media Outlays: ₱900.00 (Two high-speed 64GB USB flash drives for secondary offline database backups).
Operational Outlays: ₱10,700.00 (Client site travel to Tondo, Manila, testing supplies, printing, and contingency).
Software Engineering Labor Valuation (650 Total Team Hours):
To ensure academic consistency across the thesis, project plan, source code documentation, and oral defense, the following terminology standards are strictly enforced:
| Offline-first client with local transaction queueing
| Host MySQL database as single authoritative store
| UUIDv4 client transaction ID + Database uniqueness constraint

tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` steers a running child at its nearest step boundary or starts a turn for an idle or ready child, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

Call with no arguments to list registered providers, with `provider` to list its advertised models, or with `provider` and `model` to inspect that exact model and its reasoning efforts. Catalog membership is advisory: an adapter may accept an unlisted model id. Use the returned ids with a delegation tool's `provider`, `model`, and `reasoning_effort` fields.

When a file you create or update is an output the user asked to receive, you must call present after writing it and before your final response, including files created through Bash or code execution. Mentioning its path in your reply does not replace this call. The files must already exist. The user opens the current source files; their contents are not copied or preserved.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$env:DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

tools.description: Send a message to a direct continuable child by its agent id. If you are a resident continuable child, you may also target your direct parent. If the target is still working, the message steers its nearest step; if it is idle, the message starts a turn. This call returns no answer from the agent — only confirmation that the message was delivered. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` steers the child's nearest step while it is running and starts a turn while it is idle. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result. Child LLM selection is optional. Omit `provider`, `model`, and `reasoning_effort` to use configured child defaults and inherit compatible missing values from the parent Agent. Supply `provider` and `model` together after using `list_subagent_models` to inspect advertised routes and efforts. tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

Act as a Senior Full-Stack Engineer specializing in PHP 8, MySQL, and React 19.

I need you to generate the complete production code for the **User Authentication & Session Management Module** for VenueVue (Document Revision 2.3). This module must run entirely offline on a local XAMPP stack over LAN (`http://192.168.137.1`).

### TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS & CONSTRAINTS
1. **No Cloud / No Supabase:** Eliminate all third-party/cloud auth dependencies. Authentication must be 100% self-hosted on PHP 8 + MySQL 8.
2. **Database Structure:**
   - `users`: `user_id`, `username`, `password_hash`, `role` (ENUM: 'BARISTA', 'OWNER'), `is_active`
   - `api_sessions`: `session_id`, `user_id`, `token_hash` (CHAR(64) SHA-256 digest), `tablet_id`, `issued_at`, `expires_at`
   - `audit_logs`: `audit_log_id`, `user_id`, `action` ('LOGIN_OK', 'LOGIN_FAIL', 'RBAC_DENIED'), `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `details`, `ip_address`, `created_at`
3. **Roles & Permissions:** Role vocabulary is strictly `'BARISTA'` and `'OWNER'`.
4. **Security Standard:** Use native `password_verify()` for password checking. Store ONLY the SHA-256 hash of the bearer token in `api_sessions`. Do not store raw tokens. Include CORS restricted to `http://192.168.137.1`.

---

### REQUIRED CODE DELIVERABLES

Please generate the following 4 production-ready, fully commented files:

#### 1. Backend Endpoint: `backend/auth.php`
- Accepts `POST` requests with JSON payload: `{ "username": "...", "password": "...", "tablet_id": "T-01" }`.
- Verifies credentials against `users.password_hash`.
- On success:
  - Generates a cryptographically secure 64-character hex token (`bin2hex(random_bytes(32))`).
  - Hashes the token with SHA-256 and inserts a record into `api_sessions` (expires in 24 hours).
  - Writes an `audit_logs` entry with `action = 'LOGIN_OK'`.
  - Returns `HTTP 200` with JSON: `{ "success": true, "token": "<raw_token>", "user": { "user_id": 1, "username": "...", "role": "BARISTA" } }`.
- On failure:
  - Writes an `audit_logs` entry with `action = 'LOGIN_FAIL'`.
  - Returns `HTTP 401` with JSON: `{ "success": false, "error": "Invalid username or password" }`.

#### 2. Backend Middleware: `backend/auth_middleware.php`
- Reusable PHP function `authenticate_request(PDO $pdo): array`.
- Reads `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from HTTP headers.
- Hashes the token with SHA-256 and queries `api_sessions` joined with `users`.
- Checks expiration (`expires_at > NOW()`) and user status (`is_active = 1`).
- Returns `['user_id' => ..., 'role' => ..., 'tablet_id' => ...]` on success.
- Automatically calls `fail(401, 'Invalid or expired session token')` on failure and logs `RBAC_DENIED` to `audit_logs`.

#### 3. Frontend Auth Context: `src/context/AuthContext.jsx` (React 19)
- Manages `user`, `token`, `isAuthenticated`, and `isLoading` states.
- Persists `token` and `user` to browser `localStorage`.
- Provides `login(username, password, tabletId)` and `logout()` functions.
- Includes a custom `fetchWithAuth(url, options)` utility wrapper that automatically attaches `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to outgoing API calls.

#### 4. Frontend UI Component: `src/components/LoginForm.jsx` (React 19 + Tailwind CSS 4)
- Touch-friendly layout tailored for tablet POS usage (minimum 48px touch targets, high contrast).
- Includes inputs for Username, Password, and Tablet Identifier (e.g., `T-01`).
- Implements error handling, loading states during network requests, and auto-redirection based on user role (`/pos` for `BARISTA`, `/admin` for `OWNER`).
